translationRepairs: In his thirteenth year he died on the road at Guizhou, aged forty; he was buried at Ruiling, posthumously made Prince of Lu with the posthumous name Xiangmu.
In the thirteenth year he died on the road at Guizhou, aged forty; he was buried at Ruiling, posthumously made Prince of Lu with the posthumous name Xiangmu.
Chinese 十三年 is a regnal year (Tianhui 13), not 'his thirteenth year', which wrongly suggests age.
Bachao was sent to strike the Song emperor at Yangzhou; the Song court got wind of it and crossed the river the night before he arrived.
Bachao and others were sent to strike the Song ruler at Yangzhou; the Song ruler heard of it and, the night before Bachao reached Yangzhou, had already crossed the Yangtze.
Omits 等 ('and others') and replaces 宋主 with 'Song court' in the second clause, losing the ruler as subject.
Ritual Department Director Li Bangzhi and Vice Director Li Shan lost one grade; Vice Minister of Rites Wu Zhicai, Director Zhang Ziyu, and Academician Zhang Ju lost two.
Ritual Department Director Li Bangzhi and Vice Director Li Shan lost one grade; Chamberlain for Ceremonials Wu Zhicai, Court of Imperial Sacrifices Director Zhang Ziyu, and Erudite Zhang Ju lost two.
太常少卿/太常丞 are Court of Imperial Sacrifices offices, not the Ritual Department (禮部); conflating them with 'Rites' is misleading.
In the fifth month, on renyin, he was made crown prince, and Shizong said to him, "Ritual honors the legitimate heir—that is why you are named.
In the fifth month, on renyin, he was made crown prince, and Shizong said to him, "Ritual honors the legitimate heir—that is why you are set up.
Chinese has 世守 (likely 世宗); English already has Shizong. Closing quote incomplete vs Chinese clause boundary is OK; 'named' understates 立卿 'installed you'.

In the eighth month of the tenth year, at the classics lecture in Chenghua Hall, Crown Prince Grand Guardian Prince Shou Shuang said, "Your Highness is still weak in our tongue—why not dismiss the Han officials around you and use only Jurchens?"

In the eighth month of the tenth year, while the crown prince was at the classics lecture in Chenghua Hall, Crown Prince Grand Guardian Prince Shou Shuang said, "Your Highness is still weak in our tongue—why not dismiss the Han officials around you and use only Jurchens?"
Chinese 帝在承華殿經筵 states the heir was at the lecture; the idiomatic omits that subject and can be read as if only Shuang is located there.
Shizong said: "When ordinary men adopt a son, they all hope that in old age he will prove useful.
Shizong said: "When ordinary men raise a son, they all hope that in old age he will prove useful.
Chinese 養子 here means rearing a son, not legal adoption; the idiomatic correctly has 'raise a son'.
Third month: Shizong went to the Upper Capital as above; the Heir guarded the realm and remained at Zhongdu.
Third month: Shizong went to the Upper Capital; the Heir guarded the realm and remained at Zhongdu.
Chinese 如上京 means went to the Upper Capital (如 = go to); as above mistranslates 如.
Since taking the regency he had been deeply modest: palace officers did not bow in court; at memorials he did not stand by; new-moon and full-moon audiences were suspended.
Since taking the regency he had been deeply modest: palace officers did not bow in court; when presenting affairs they did not stand in attendance; new-moon and full-moon audiences were suspended.
啟事時不侍立 takes palace officers as subject; they did not stand attendant, not the heir.

Shizong put Prince of Bin Yongcheng in charge at the Central Capital, sent Zai Xing, chief steward of the Prince of Teng’s house, and Palace Service Commissioner Alila to guard the Prince of Jinyuan, sent Left Imperial Wardrobe Commissioner Tangkuo Ding with offerings, and ordered Consort Tudan and the imperial grandsons to mourn by Han custom.

Shizong put Prince of Bin Yongcheng in charge at the Central Capital, sent Zai Xing, chief steward of the Prince of Teng’s house, and Palace Service Commissioner Alila to guard the Prince of Jinyuan, sent Left Xuanhui Commissioner Tangkuo Ding with offerings, and ordered Consort Tudan and the imperial grandsons to mourn by Han custom.
左宣徽使 is Left Xuanhui Commissioner, not an Imperial Wardrobe office.
When property was lost he made the loser pay compensation but imposed no further penalty.
When property was lost he made those responsible for the loss pay compensation but imposed no further penalty.
亡失物者 means the party responsible for losing the goods; 'the loser' is ambiguous and can reverse the sense.

When Empress Mingde was buried at Kunhou and consorts were enshrined with her, the procession left Panning Palace; Prince of Zhao Wei Zhong sent his mother’s bier ahead and yellow canopies forward; the emperor called the bearers and got no answer; Junior Palace Steward Zhang Jinyan would have reported it, but the emperor stopped him.

When Empress Mingde was buried at Kunhou and consorts were enshrined with her, the procession left Panning Palace; Wei Zhong, Prince of Zhao, sent his mother’s bier ahead and yellow canopies forward; the emperor called the bearers and got no answer; Junior Palace Steward Zhang Jinyan would have reported it, but the emperor stopped him.
趙王惟中 is title plus personal name Wei Zhong; 'Prince of Zhao Wei Zhong' wrongly reads Zhao as part of the personal name.
Comment: Prince of Liao Gao took the Zhong Capital; Zonghan and Zongwang followed, while Jingxuan separately led the hezha meng'an.
Comment: Gao, Prince of Liao, took the Zhong Capital; Zonghan and Zongwang followed, while Jingxuan separately led the hezha meng'an.
遼王杲 is title plus personal name Gao; 'Prince of Liao Gao' wrongly reads Liao as part of the personal name.
